packageRules.description: LibreChat itself. Never automerge. Pinning this image to a release tag is the whole reason Renovate is here: the previous deployment tracked a `:latest` tag, drifted onto a pre-release, and stayed several versions behind without anyone deciding to. A pinned tag plus a pull request makes every upgrade a choice somebody made.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Read https://www.librechat.ai/changelog from the current version forward before merging.
Diff the new release's own `librechat.example.yaml` against this repository's `librechat.yaml`. Renamed and removed keys are the most common upgrade break and prose changelogs miss them.
Check whether the `version:` key at the top of `librechat.yaml` changed.
Check for NEW REQUIRED environment variables. `ADMIN_PANEL_SESSION_SECRET` was one of these in v0.8.7 and the admin panel refuses to start without it.
Check whether the upstream organization or registry path changed. The org was renamed from danny-avila to LibreChat-AI in 2026, and the old image path silently stopped receiving releases.

packageRules.description: Supporting services. Grouped so they arrive as one pull request rather than four, and still reviewed by a person.

MongoDB and Meilisearch MAJOR versions are disabled deliberately, not forgotten. Both hold state that a major version can refuse to read: a Mongo major needs a documented, tested upgrade path with a restore point ready, and Meilisearch encodes its version in the data directory path, so a bump silently starts with an empty index. Neither belongs in an automated pull request. Minor and patch updates still come through.

MongoDB and Meilisearch minor/patch updates. Meilisearch minor bumps still need the data directory path in compose.yaml updated to match, or the index rebuilds from scratch — which is safe, but slow and surprising if unexpected.
prBodyNotes: For Meilisearch: update the `${DATA_DIR}/meili_data_vX.Y.Z` volume path in compose.yaml to match the new version. The index rebuilds from MongoDB on first start, which is expected and takes a few minutes.

packageRules.description: Code interpreter (optional module): upstream's own images. Disabled on purpose. Upstream publishes them only as `sha-<commit>` tags with no version tags and no `latest`, so codeinterpreter/compose.yaml pins bare digests and Renovate has no version to compare. Bumps are manual; docs/modules/code-interpreter.md has the procedure, including running a REAL execution first (v1.10.4 passed every health check and failed every execution).
Code interpreter (optional module): its supporting services. Their state is disposable (24-hour session files), so a format change costs a volume reset, not data.
prBodyNotes: Deploys only to the code interpreter VM, through its own deploy timer.
Garage: if a release changes the metadata format and Garage refuses to start, remove the `garage_meta` and `garage_data` volumes on the interpreter VM. Session files are disposable.
rclone: it runs codeinterpreter/file-cleanup/file-cleanup.sh. Check that the `delete`, `lsf`, `--min-age` and `--use-server-modtime` flags are unchanged.
After it deploys, upload a file through Run Code and confirm it round-trips. Health checks alone do not prove the file path.

packageRules.description: The MCP tool servers, each published from its own public repository. Pinned to release tags so that what this deployment runs is always a specific reviewed build.
GitHub Actions used by the workflows. Low risk and high noise, so patch and minor updates merge themselves once CI is green.
